executive_summary: US military strikes on Iran entered their second day, keeping Brent crude near $95 and WTI at $92 as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic. Yesterday's CPI print showed headline inflation at 4.2% YoY driven by energy, but core CPI undershot at 0.2% MoM, giving the Fed room to hold at next week's FOMC. The ECB is expected to hike 25bps to 2.25% today — its first increase since 2023 — responding to the same energy-driven inflation. Semiconductors are recovering from last week's $1.4T selloff, with Nasdaq futures up 1.24% premarket. Trump announced a China trade deal maintaining 30% tariffs with a 60-day pause on escalation, providing a modest tailwind.

macro_events.title: US Strikes Iran — Day 2; Strait of Hormuz Near-Closure
macro_events.causal_chain: US strikes Iranian installations in Hormozgan province → Iran retaliates with missile attacks on US naval assets and closes Strait of Hormuz → 21% of global oil trade and 20% of LNG transits disrupted → war-risk insurance on VLCCs becomes prohibitive → commercial shipping reroutes via Cape of Good Hope (+10-14 days, +$2M/trip) → Brent surges to $95, WTI to $92 → energy CPI component already 60%+ of headline inflation → Asian refiners and European gas buyers scramble for alternatives → Dutch TTF gas futures spike → tanker day-rates surge on rerouting demand
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, global energy supply chains, Europe (gas), Asia (refining)
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent +15% in 24h, tanker stocks ran 20-35% in one week. Current situation is more severe due to sustained Hormuz closure vs one-off facility strike.
macro_events.counterargument: Limited oil volumes still transiting the Gulf; US Strategic Petroleum Reserve could release; Iran has economic incentive to reopen Hormuz quickly to maintain its own oil exports

macro_events.title: May CPI: Headline 4.2% YoY, Core Undershoot at 0.2% MoM
macro_events.causal_chain: CPI headline at 4.2% driven by energy (+3.9% MoM) → confirms Iran-driven supply shock is the inflation story → BUT core CPI at 0.2% MoM undershot consensus → shelter cooling to 0.3% MoM → signals underlying demand-pull inflation is contained → traders pare back rate hike expectations → 2Y yield drops 2bps to 4.15% → Fed has room to hold at June 16-17 FOMC → risk assets find support on dovish interpretation of core → however headline stays politically toxic for Fed credibility
macro_events.historical_analog: 2022 energy-driven CPI spikes — Fed ultimately looked through supply shocks initially before pivoting hawkish. Current dynamic similar but Fed already at 3.5-3.75%.
macro_events.counterargument: If PPI today prints hot (April was 6.0% YoY), the benign core CPI narrative breaks down and rate hike expectations re-accelerate

affected_tickers.reason: Core CPI relief vs headline inflation pressure

macro_events.title: ECB Expected to Hike 25bps to 2.25% — First Hike Since 2023
macro_events.time_horizon: Intraday, with forward guidance implications for weeks
macro_events.causal_chain: Energy shock from Hormuz closure transmits to European gas prices → eurozone headline inflation accelerates → ECB signals hike at April meeting → 99.6% market-implied probability of 25bps to 2.25% → EUR/USD likely strengthens on rate differential narrowing → European bank margins improve on higher rates → but European growth outlook darkens as energy costs weigh on manufacturing → DAX and industrial names vulnerable
macro_events.historical_analog: ECB hike cycle 2022-2023 — deposit rate went from -0.5% to 4.0%. This reversal after cutting cycle signals policy regime change.
macro_events.counterargument: Hike is fully priced; forward guidance and tone on future hikes matters more than the decision itself

affected_tickers.reason: German industrials hurt by energy costs + tighter policy

macro_events.title: May PPI Release at 8:30 AM ET
macro_events.causal_chain: April PPI printed 6.0% YoY (highest since Dec 2022) → if May PPI accelerates, it confirms cost-push inflation pipeline → corporate margin compression ahead → strengthens case for Fed hike → 10Y yield pushes above 4.55% resistance → growth stocks sell off → BUT if PPI decelerates, confirms benign core CPI signal and risk rallies
macro_events.historical_analog: PPI leads CPI by 1-2 months in cost-push cycles. Hot PPI in April correctly predicted hot headline CPI in May.
macro_events.counterargument: Markets may look through PPI if clearly energy-driven, as core CPI already provided relief

affected_tickers.reason: Hot PPI sends yields higher, bond prices lower
Growth names de-rate on yield spike if PPI hot

macro_events.title: Trump Announces China Trade Deal — 30% Tariff Maintained, 60-Day Pause
macro_events.causal_chain: Deal maintains 20% fentanyl + 10% reciprocal tariffs (30% total) → pauses further escalation for 60 days → reduces tail risk of tariff spiral → marginal positive for supply chain certainty → US importers get temporary cost stability → Chinese export stocks find floor → but 30% is still historically high → no structural resolution

macro_events.counterargument: 60-day pause is just a can-kick; structural issues remain unresolved
